title: KL Rahul Out Hit Wicket for Four After Duck as India A Fight Back in Lincoln
excerpt: Rahul was dismissed by Fraser Sheat twice — edging behind for a duck, then hitting his own stumps trying to stop a rolling ball — while Padikkal and Sudharsan took India A to 106 for 2, trailing New Zealand A by 98.
body:
• KL Rahul scored 0 off 8 balls in the first innings and 4 off 15 in the second, dismissed by Fraser Sheat both times in the first unofficial Test against New Zealand A at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval in Lincoln.
  • His second dismissal was hit wicket: he defended, the ball rolled slowly back, and in trying to stop it his bat struck the off stump — replays showed the ball was not heading for the stumps.
  • India A were bowled out for 113, New Zealand A made 317 for a 204-run lead, and Devdutt Padikkal (56 not out) and Sai Sudharsan (39 not out) took India A to 106 for 2 at stumps on Day 2, still trailing by 98 runs.
  • The match is not finished — the second unofficial Test starts October 31, ahead of the senior team's two-Test series in New Zealand starting November 19 in Wellington.

A duck, then a dismissal he inflicted on himself

KL Rahul endured a match to forget in the first unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval. After a duck in the first innings, he made just four runs off 15 balls in the second before a bizarre hit-wicket dismissal against fast bowler Fraser Sheat, according to CricketAddictor.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=9piH8_-qMdQ

"The ball dropped onto the pitch and rolled slowly back towards him."

In the fifth over of the second innings, Rahul leaned forward to a good-length delivery outside off stump and defended with soft hands. The ball dropped onto the pitch and rolled slowly back towards him. Trying to keep it away from the stumps, he reached with his bat and accidentally struck the off stump, dislodging the bails. Side-on replays showed the ball was not heading for the stumps at all. Rahul pointed his bat towards the umpire and non-striker Devdutt Padikkal to indicate what had happened, then walked off visibly frustrated — dismissed by Sheat for the second time in the match.

How India A fell for 113

The first innings set the tone. On a green pitch on Saturday, October 24, Rahul edged a Sheat delivery that moved away to wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay after facing eight balls without scoring. Yashasvi Jaiswal made 17 off 45, Padikkal resisted with 32 off 77, and Yash Rathod finished unbeaten on 44, but India A were bowled out for 113. Simon Keene took 5 for 24 and Zak Gibson 3 for 29 for New Zealand A.

https://x.com/lightningspeedk/status/2114225876112122059

New Zealand A then built a commanding reply. Rhys Mariu and Curtis Heaphy added 132 for the opening wicket before Mukesh Choudhary dismissed Mariu for 76. Auqib Nabi struck twice in successive deliveries to leave the hosts 135 for 3 at stumps on Day 1, but the tail resisted on Day 2: Dean Foxcroft made 51 and Kristian Clarke 42 as New Zealand A reached 317, a lead of 204. Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi took three wickets each for India A, as detailed in the Khel Ja match report.

Padikkal and Sudharsan fight back

India A's second innings began badly again. Jaiswal, who had made 17 in the first innings, was out for 5 when a short delivery from Keene thudded into his glove and flew to Hay. Rahul followed soon after with his hit-wicket dismissal, leaving the visitors in deep trouble still well behind.

Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan then dug in. Mixing caution with aggression, they survived probing spells and took India A to 106 for 2 at stumps on Day 2, with Padikkal unbeaten on 56 and Sudharsan on 39. India A still trail by 98 runs, so the pair's work is only a start — but it turned a potential innings defeat into a contest, and both are among the batters in contention for places in the senior Test series that follows.

What it means for Rahul and what comes next

For Rahul, the scores matter because this series is preparation, not a trial in isolation. He was expected to use the A tour to find red-ball rhythm before joining the senior team, and instead he leaves Lincoln with 4 runs from two innings and a dismissal that will be replayed for the wrong reasons. One bad match does not decide a senior place, but it removes the form argument he could have carried into selection discussions.

The three-match unofficial Test series continues with the second match starting October 31 and the third on November 7. After that, the senior Indian team faces New Zealand in two Tests — the first starting November 19 in Wellington and the second on November 27 in Christchurch. India A first have a third day to save this match: Padikkal and Sudharsan need to bat deep, and the middle order needs to erase the remaining 98-run deficit before India A can think about setting any target at all.
